walkthroughs.body_html:
Chemical Reactions — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Chemical Reactions brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Chemical Reactions.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Limewater turns cloudy in the presence of:
What kind of bond forms between a ligand and a central metal ion in a complex?
options: The ligand shares electrons equally with the metal as a normal covalent bond.
A dative (coordinate) covalent bond — the ligand donates a lone pair into an empty orbital on the metal.
A strong acid is one that has been heated to higher temperature.
The ligand forms an ionic bond with the metal because the metal is positively charged.

mcqs.q: How is a dynamic equilibrium different from a static one?
options: Dynamic and static equilibria are the same thing because both show constant macroscopic properties.
The ligand shares electrons equally with the metal as a normal covalent bond.
In a dynamic equilibrium, forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates; in a static equilibrium, nothing is happening at the particle level.
A dynamic equilibrium means the system is still changing visibly.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a strong acid and a concentrated acid?
options: A dynamic equilibrium means the system is still changing visibly.
A strong acid fully dissociates in water; a concentrated acid has a high amount of acid per volume — these are independent properties.
A strong acid is one that has been heated to higher temperature.
Strong and concentrated mean the same thing for acids.
